# Protocol fixtures

These are synthetic public-data fixtures with the shapes documented by Hyperliquid's [perpetual metadata](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/info-endpoint/perpetuals), [L2 snapshots](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/info-endpoint#l2-book-snapshot), and [WebSocket subscriptions](https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/websocket/subscriptions).

Values and addresses are test data, not captured accounts or market observations. Trailing decimal zeros, a large native trade ID, and unknown metadata fields deliberately exercise lossless decoding. No secret material is present.

`account.json` and `open_orders.json` are also synthetic. They cover signed positions, nullable liquidation prices, exact margin strings, and order IDs beyond JavaScript's exact integer range. Their shapes follow the native perpetual account and open-order endpoints.

## Signing reference

`signing_vectors.json` contains 36 L1-action vectors and 8 user-signed vectors generated by the [official Hyperliquid Python SDK](https://github.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyperliquid-python-sdk/tree/2fdb18f9517675ea03695a0962bd19eece9c83f0), pinned to revision `2fdb18f9517675ea03695a0962bd19eece9c83f0`.

The fixture records SHA-256 hashes of the signing/type source files and the oracle package versions. It uses the same **public test private key** found in the reference SDK's signing tests; it is test data, not a workspace credential. Fixture signatures and digests are computed by the Python reference, independently of the Rust implementation.

Coverage includes both networks, vault presence, expiry, limit/trigger orders, client IDs, builder/sub-builder fields, priority grouping, 64-bit cancellation IDs, and both signature domains. Offline tests compare MessagePack bytes, hashes, digests, signatures, and recovered addresses, and reject altered context or invalid signatures. User-signed vectors cover `UsdSend` and `ApproveAgent`; this does not add transfer or approval submission APIs.

To regenerate from the connectors directory using a dedicated development environment:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv-oracle
.venv-oracle/bin/pip install -r scripts/signing-oracle-requirements.txt
.venv-oracle/bin/python scripts/signing_vectors.py
```

The generator downloads only pinned reference files and records their hashes. It is an explicit development tool; normal tests read the checked-in JSON without Python crypto packages or network access. No Python SDK or signing oracle is a Rust runtime dependency.
